title: Sain full Verifiable Intelligence Stack audit
completion_rule: Every requirement must be satisfied, or carry an explicit user-accepted waiver. Bounded demonstrations, absent capabilities, external dependencies, and open research do not count as complete.

requirements.requirement: Maintain distinct but connected execution and epistemic graphs
requirements.evidence: A separately sealed EpistemicGraph persists canonical claims with evidence, assumption, falsifier, policy, and execution-lineage edges; model interrogation records are linked into it and state loading rejects nested or re-sealed claim mutation

requirements.requirement: Represent computational, provenance, epistemic, and normative validity separately
requirements.evidence: Every canonical EpistemicClaim contains four separately typed validity statuses plus a scope statement and distinct evidence/execution/policy relations; validation forbids elevating uncalibrated model inference to epistemically verified merely because execution or provenance is supported

requirements.requirement: Operate approximate and exact computational planes through a formally certified boundary
requirements.evidence: The original rational quantized-linear certificate is now complemented by a complete bounded quantized transformer block. Its checked-i128 plane performs Q/K/V projection, deterministic hard-attention selection, residuals, ReLU feed-forward projection, and authoritative output; an independently implemented binary64 plane is accepted only when every attention decision and activation exactly agrees. Model version, weight/source/dependency/data identities and private-input/public-output commitments are sealed, Rust replay and an independent Python implementation reject mutation, and the certificate states its exact arithmetic bound and excludes softmax, arbitrary accelerators, and zk privacy from scope.

requirements.requirement: Bind model, inputs, numerical profile, error region, deterministic policy, evaluation, and lineage in each authoritative claim
requirements.evidence: AuthoritativeClaimCertificate binds model, parameters, inputs, data lineage, numerical and hardware profiles, error region, deterministic policy, evaluation conditions, and execution lineage into one sealed object. EpistemicGraph rejects authoritative claims without the certificate, exact execution/policy links, verified computational/provenance/normative status, and calibrated confidence for model inference; advisory model responses cannot masquerade as authoritative

requirements.requirement: Provide native incremental verification for long-running accepted state transitions
requirements.evidence: Alongside the legacy commitment accumulator, sain-ivc now provides a Nova-folded accepted-state circuit that constrains predecessor generation/state equality, exactly-one generation advancement, checked affine state semantics, claimed-after equality, mandatory authorization acceptance, and a Poseidon authorization-lineage root at every step. Extension starts from the prior verified output, maintains constant proof size in tests, and rejects discontinuity, arithmetic forgery, false authorization, proof mutation, and final-state mutation. The CLI supports create/extend/verify; the formal statement and trusted boundary are documented.

requirements.requirement: Report honest scale metrics including represented domain, evaluated constraints, field operations, memory, proof size, verifier time, and energy
requirements.evidence: The Power House scale benchmark now emits an HONEST_SCALE_METRICS record on every run and optionally archives JSON. It separately reports 2^n notation and decimal domain points, unique processed points, evaluator invocations, evaluated constraints with protocol scope, derived prover/verifier field operations excluding evaluator arithmetic, canonical proof bytes, prover/verifier nanoseconds, peak RSS with source, and measured energy or an explicit unavailable reason without estimates. A checked-in measured artifact and independent formula/schema tests are present.

requirements.requirement: Use portable proof-carrying state capsules containing complete model, learning, evaluation, environmental, policy, safety, expiry, and revocation state
requirements.evidence: ProofCarryingIntelligenceCapsule wraps the exact portable state/journal capsule in a mandatory typed manifest binding model state, optimizer state or explicit non-applicability, source and dependency identities, training/self-modification lineage, evaluations, challenge vectors, epistemic uncertainty, grounded environmental observations, constitution/policy, protected safety constraints, exclusive expiry/no-expiry policy, and the verified revocation registry. Cross-context challenge substitution and invalid/revoked packaging fail.

requirements.requirement: Enforce epistemic types for observation, testimony, inference, deduction, simulation, counterfactual, policy, and hypothesis
requirements.evidence: Closed EvidenceType enum, proof-bound metadata, forbidden elevation, expiry and revocation tests

requirements.requirement: Translate Rootprint/capsule provenance to and from W3C PROV
requirements.evidence: Verified capsule export produces PROV-JSON entities, activities, agents, derivations, usage, generation, and association relations; fail-closed import recovers the exact Sain binding and rejects nested and re-sealed substitutions

requirements.requirement: Interoperate with SLSA and in-toto provenance without losing Sain identity
requirements.evidence: The same deterministic bundle emits an in-toto Statement v1 with SLSA provenance v1 buildDefinition/runDetails, capsule subject, state/journal dependencies, and loss-detecting round-trip tests

requirements.requirement: Create every proposed self-modification as an isolated lineage fork
requirements.evidence: Authoritative state rejects direct mutation and requires an exact verified unrevoked capsule fork

requirements.requirement: Require static/formal checks, reproducible evaluation, adversarial tests, capability/safety regression, distribution shift, resource accounting, authorization, delay, and rollback before promotion
requirements.evidence: Schema-2 self-modifications cannot reach evaluated or promoted state without a sealed seven-stage PromotionEvaluationManifest; constitutional authorization, minimum delay, and exact rollback are separately mandatory. Cognitive-dynamics promotion runs shifted-seed testing and measured resource accounting; deterministic merge permits only a reason-bound distribution-shift N/A. Rust and independent Python tests reject missing, failed, mutated, and cross-bound stages

requirements.requirement: Use formal, empirical, adversarial, human/institutional, and meta-evaluators
requirements.evidence: Formal/synthetic evaluators, distinct signed evaluators, and meta-evaluator forgery rejection
requirements.gap: No independent human or institutional evaluator is integrated.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate useful self-improvement without loss of identity, accountability, or reversibility
requirements.evidence: A bounded quantized-transformer update now provides a falsifiable useful-improvement demonstration: exhaustive deterministic replay selects one weight change, reduces squared error from 2 to 1, binds parent/candidate/data/evaluation identities, creates an isolated fork, and retains the exact parent model as rollback. The machine constitution separates proposal, evaluation, and promotion authority; a delayed promoted record and a separately rejected regression-control record are embedded in docs/governed_update/ceremony.json. The complete ceremony reconstructs byte-for-byte and rejects rollback mutation. Its non-claim explicitly limits the result to one bounded update rather than general self-improvement.

requirements.requirement: Represent persistent objects, physical constraints, agents, incentives, causal mechanisms, time, conservation, uncertainty, and competing hypotheses
requirements.evidence: A persisted GroundedWorldModel has explicit proof-bound types for persistent objects and agents, physical and conservation constraints with units, agent incentives, causal mechanisms and interventions, temporal order, calibrated measurement uncertainty, and competing falsifiable hypotheses. Organism loading validates the model digest and ontology version; Rust tests populate every required category and reject resealed ontology tampering.

requirements.requirement: Generalize causal and counterfactual reasoning under interventions and distribution shift
requirements.evidence: Alongside the preregistered synthetic known/held-out mechanism protocol, benchmarks/real_world_causal_2026-07-31.json evaluates a real randomized intervention and two real observational population shifts using the NBER-hosted National Supported Work/LaLonde data. A deterministic standardized nearest-neighbor counterfactual model is evaluated against the randomized treatment-effect reference after replacing experimental controls with PSID and CPS controls. It reduces reference error by 89.14% and 95.47%, respectively, versus the preregistered unadjusted observational baseline. Source URLs and SHA-256 identities, license, covariates, method, baseline, gate, limitations, and non-persistence of restricted raw data are bound. The report explicitly denies individual counterfactual truth or universal open-world generalization.

requirements.requirement: Attach model version, initial conditions, assumptions, interventions, randomness, approximation, confidence, and failure domains to every simulation
requirements.evidence: GroundedWorldModel accepts only sealed SimulationEnvelopes with every required field and cross-model substitution rejection. All six planner families, active/noisy causal benchmarks, incremental causal learning, and native structural causal discovery return mandatory result-bound envelopes carrying model material, initial commitment, assumptions, interventions, randomness, numerical profile, confidence, failure domains, result, and execution lineage; arena aggregation retains every nested causal envelope. The checked-in simulation registry classifies all eleven authoritative paths and a CI test rejects any new unregistered `fn simulate` definition or removal of required fields. Replay verifiers reject absent and mutated envelopes; the registry expressly disclaims an ability to detect deliberately misclassified future semantics.

requirements.requirement: Provide a bidirectional neural-to-symbolic-to-test-to-update interface with source linkage
requirements.evidence: A canonical protocol now seals neural model/state/input/output identities into a hypothesis, derives an assumption/falsifier-bearing symbolic proposition, preregisters evaluator/protocol/hidden cases before reveal, binds disposition and uncertainty, and emits one receipt linking both neural and symbolic before/after states under an update policy. Reveal substitution and re-sealed cross-link tampering fail

requirements.requirement: Run across heterogeneous digital, tensor, photonic, neuromorphic, in-memory, enclave, finite-field, reversible, or quantum-assisted hardware as appropriate
requirements.evidence: The transformer boundary now runs on the checked integer CPU path, binary64 CPU path, independent Python path, and a physical discrete AMD Turks GPU through an OpenGL 4.3 compute shader, in addition to prior virtualized cross-architecture conformance. The physical GPU is identified by PCI 1002:6740 and radeon/Mesa evidence rather than renderer assertion alone.
requirements.gap: This establishes physical CPU/GPU heterogeneity only. No tensor-core, photonic, neuromorphic, in-memory, enclave, reversible, or quantum-assisted integration is present.

requirements.requirement: Provide a deterministic digital shadow for approximate devices including identity, firmware, calibration, commitments, error bounds, environment, faults, and reference relation
requirements.evidence: docs/physical_gpu_shadow_conformance.json is a replayed certificate for the physical AMD Turks GPU approximate plane. A GLSL compute shader executes Q/K/V projections, hard attention, residuals, and feed-forward operations; every attention choice and quantized activation exactly matches the checked-i128 CPU and independent Python reference. The shadow seals PCI/device/driver identity, explicit firmware-unavailability evidence, known-vector calibration, private-input/public-output commitments, declared and observed zero error bound, boot/display/architecture environment, GL fault state, source and compiled-binary identities, and the deterministic acceptance relation. Physical rerun passes; re-sealed device, output, bound, and fault mutations fail.

requirements.requirement: Bind joules, power, heat, cooling, water, carbon, wear, networking, proof overhead, and expected value to significant transitions
requirements.evidence: Every new authoritative transition ResourceReceipt now commits joules and source or explicit absence; derived average power and heat upper-bound accounting when energy exists; cooling, water, carbon, hardware wear, network bytes, proof time/energy overhead, and expected value as typed metric evidence. Each metric must be a sourced bound value or `unavailable_not_estimated` with a reason—silent estimates are invalid. Legacy receipts remain verifiable through omitted optional fields, the independent Python verifier reconstructs field order and validates availability semantics, and transition mutation tests pass.

requirements.requirement: Schedule computation by grid carbon, renewable availability, cooling, latency, residency, verification, specialization, and reliability
requirements.evidence: The native deterministic scheduler hard-enforces region, specialization, capacity, latency, and reliability, then minimizes an overflow-checked integer objective covering carbon, renewable share, cooling PUE, latency, verification energy, and reliability. It records every rejected and eligible alternative, binds site evidence, replays exactly, and rejects metric, policy, or selection mutation. A standalone JSON CLI is included

requirements.requirement: Optimize and report reliable verified intelligence per joule and scarce material
requirements.evidence: The operational sain-efficiency interface reports exact rational metrics for challenge-weighted verified useful outcomes per measured joule and per material-service unit, binds workload/evaluator/inventory identities, refuses zero or estimated energy, and deterministically selects the maximum joint efficiency with overflow-checked cross multiplication. Its scope statement explicitly prevents presentation as a universal intelligence measure; replay and tamper tests pass.

requirements.requirement: Establish trusted sensing from phenomenon through identity, calibration, time, context, health, tamper evidence, sampling, raw data, transforms, uncertainty, and corroboration
requirements.evidence: The physical CMOS RTC/NTP conformance chain now covers one real attached phenomenon end to end. Schema 2 binds RTC identity/device path/clocksource/boot, signed Ed25519 origin, NTP server/stratum/reference/distance/offset/jitter calibration, physical battery and 24-hour health, runtime state and cross-clock self-test, sampling method/interfaces/count, raw RTC/realtime/monotonic/driver data, midpoint and uncertainty transforms, minimized location context, read-only-interface and signed-origin tamper evidence, faults, and three independent time bases. Hardware-attestation absence is explicit rather than fabricated. The generic TrustedSensorReading separately enforces the same full vocabulary for other sensor types. Physical capture and independent verification pass; raw, calibration, context, and signature mutations fail.

requirements.requirement: Bind consequential actuation from observation through alternatives, authorization, prediction, command, receipt, outcome, and discrepancy
requirements.evidence: The fail-closed ActuationTransition cross-binds observation, model state, alternatives, prediction, policy, authorization identity, command, actuator receipt, sensor chain, measured outcome, and discrepancy. It is now attached to an actual reversible physical loop: ALSA/PipeWire commands the host's CS4206 analog speaker to emit a low-volume 937 Hz tone, the physical analog microphone records a before/intervention pair, and a preregistered correlation detector observes a 56.604x target-to-baseline-or-sideband ratio. Process receipts, ALSA identity, monotonic times, the command waveform, both raw microphone waveforms, and a consumer-device calibration limitation are preserved in docs/physical_actuation. Python and independent Rust verification accept the exact transition; a re-sealed cross-receipt substitution is rejected. This demonstrates the binding protocol on real actuation while explicitly not claiming a high-stakes institutional deployment.

requirements.requirement: Apply stronger evidence and authorization thresholds to irreversible actions
requirements.evidence: Authorization policy requires reversible actions to carry at least 0.70 evidence strength and one approval, while irreversible actions require at least 0.95 and three distinct digest-bound approvers. Tests prove that two approvals and 0.949999 evidence fail while the reversible threshold and complete irreversible threshold pass.

requirements.requirement: Operate a global independently challengeable Observatory accepting counterexamples, reproductions, alternative data, adversarial environments, safety probes, interventions, and branch inconsistencies
requirements.evidence: https://github.com/JROChub/sain-observatory is now a public, globally reachable issue-form/API intake accepting all seven required challenge classes. It warns against public secrets/personal data/harmful payloads, supports private evidence commitments and private vulnerability reporting, preserves public issue history, and uses a pinned GitHub workflow to create a data-minimized issue-body commitment, keylessly sign it through GitHub OIDC/Sigstore, verify the workflow identity, upload the receipt, and attach its digest/run to the issue. Public smoke issue 1 and run 30688603920 succeeded; the preserved receipt and bundle independently verify with Cosign 3.0.6. The service explicitly separates open challengeability from independent institutional adjudication and truth.

requirements.requirement: Prevent benchmark capture with public, private, renewed, and competing-institution tests committed before reveal
requirements.evidence: Private-then-revealed renewed signed epochs with confirmed and falsified outcomes
requirements.gap: Challenge families and institutions were project controlled.

requirements.requirement: Expose knowledge, inference, assumptions, falsifiers, failure history, version, and calibrated uncertainty with each claim
requirements.evidence: Canonical claims require an evidence type, confidence or explicit uncalibrated status, validity vector, non-empty evidence, assumptions, falsifiers, prior-failure history, execution lineage, policy references, schema, and generation. Model interrogation binds the current strategy-revocation count; missing relations and false epistemic elevation fail closed

requirements.requirement: Machine-enforce invariants, capability boundaries, modification procedures, oversight, privacy, resources, emergency interruption, appeal, fork/exit, rollback, and constitutional amendment
requirements.evidence: The existing Constitution enforces deny-by-default capabilities, separated proposer/evaluator/operator roles, resource ceilings, review, promotion delay, quorum, invariants, and rollback. The complementary signed GovernanceCharter immutably protects human oversight, privacy/minimization, emergency interruption, appeal, fork/exit, and safe amendment. It requires at least three oversight keys, blocks disclosure while halted, requires three signed approvals to resume, two for appeals, makes exit directly receiptable, and rejects rights-removing, under-delayed, under-signed amendments. Mutation and threshold tests pass.

requirements.requirement: Separate authority to predict from authority to act using explicit capabilities
requirements.evidence: Organism core lacks actuation and promotion authority; physical actuation is denied by default

requirements.requirement: Safely merge intelligent branches across state, goals, ontology, permissions, conflicts, uncertainty, provenance, invariants, capability expansion, and reversibility
requirements.evidence: The conservative three-way merge protocol proves a common ancestor, distinct branch transitions, disjoint state changes, unchanged nonempty goal, matching constitution and capability set, matching memory/epistemic/world/temporal/neural schema signatures, and either identical uncertainty graphs or a change by only one branch. It rejects conflicts, capability expansion, ontology-schema divergence, concurrent uncertainty divergence, invariant failure, and attestation-key mismatch; promotion is delayed and authorized, provenance binds both branches, and the ancestor capsule is the executable rollback. Rust replay plus an independent Python assessment/capsule verifier reject forged and cross-bound material.

requirements.requirement: Support versioned algorithms, domain separation, multi-algorithm signatures, migration proofs, re-anchoring, archival verification, explicit assumptions, and post-quantum alternatives
requirements.evidence: Versioned domain-separated ReanchorCertificates require both Ed25519 and FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 signatures over the same identity/lineage migration statement, with independent OpenSSL verification. ContinuityArchive adds an algorithm registry, standards and roles, explicit per-suite trust assumptions, canonical serialization, source/dependency bundle identity, redundant offline archival requirements, and a complete offline verification recipe. Removal of assumptions or mutation is rejected after resealing.

requirements.requirement: Obtain an independently reviewed threat model
requirements.evidence: The original threat model is now explicitly labeled internal, and a separate dated adversarial review records twelve findings, methods, limitations, acceptance tests, priorities, and a residual-risk decision.
requirements.gap: As the review itself discloses, no independent organization or outside named reviewer has signed it; internal review cannot satisfy this requirement.

requirements.requirement: Formally specify identity, fork, merge, replay, and equivalence
requirements.evidence: formal/SainIdentity.tla defines identity-preserving roots, exact forks, journal-based advancement/replay, conservative common-root merges and rollback, and an equivalence relation. The pinned official TLC 2.19 tool exhaustively checked the bounded configuration: 1,945 generated states, 1,193 distinct states, zero queued states, and no invariant errors. The report explicitly limits this to a finite abstract model and does not claim Rust refinement proof.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate cross-language and cross-platform conformance
requirements.evidence: Cross-language conformance now spans Rust authoritative implementations, independent Python replays, a C/OpenGL host, and a GLSL compute shader. Cross-platform evidence includes local Intel x86-64, AArch64/QEMU, an externally executed GitHub/Azure AMD EPYC runner, RISC-V guest execution inside RISC Zero, and a physical AMD Turks GPU with exact CPU/GPU transformer agreement. Each profile states its virtualization/administration boundary and rejects mutations; this is evidence for the declared bounded relations, not arbitrary cross-platform neural determinism.

requirements.requirement: Publish comparative benchmarks against zkVM, folding, and provenance systems
requirements.evidence: benchmarks/comparative/results_2026-07-31.json publishes a controlled, source-bound eight-transition comparison: a real RISC Zero 3.0.6 zkVM receipt (62.376 s prove, 30.660 ms verify, 221,242-byte receipt), a Nova 0.40.0 accepted-state IVC proof (13.162 s prove, 4.776 s verify, 1,672,072-byte proof), and 1,000 W3C PROV-JSON plus in-toto Statement v1 lineage encode/replay iterations. The artifact reports statement differences, peak memory, public-output size, unavailable rather than fabricated energy, exact toolchains/lock digest, and rejects universal ranking. Tests validate the published schema and deterministic provenance baseline; the benchmark sources and lock are now included in the supply-chain manifest and dependency inventory.

requirements.requirement: Publish prover, verifier, memory, proof-size, and energy measurements
requirements.evidence: docs/proof_path_registry.json enumerates all four proof implementations shipped in the source tree. benchmarks/proof_path_metrics_2026-07-31.json publishes a uniform verified record for each: prover time, verifier time, peak resident memory, serialized proof/receipt size, statement scope, source artifact, and either measured energy or an explicit unavailable_not_estimated reason. The rows cover streaming sum-check, legacy Nova commitment IVC, accepted-state Nova IVC, and a real RISC Zero guest receipt. Tests require exact registry/measurement agreement and reject missing, zero, or fabricated fields.

requirements.requirement: Provide mutation, adversarial, reproducible-build, signed-release, trusted-component, and cryptographic-agility evidence
requirements.evidence: Extensive mutation/adversarial suites, a historical two-builder byte-identical bounded binary, externally OIDC/Sigstore-signed binary and SLSA statement, and Ed25519-to-ML-DSA continuity evidence exist. The supply-chain generator now excludes secrets/private state, inventories both Rust dependency closures, every Python pin, npm lock content, llama.cpp runtime commit, and all four lockfiles; provenance commits the inventory, and a typed seven-boundary trusted-component disclosure is emitted and tested.
requirements.gap: The externally signed/reproducible artifacts are historical bounded releases rather than the current complete workspace. A current hermetic all-deliverable build, independent rebuild, dependency vulnerability review, and new external release signature are still required.

requirements.requirement: Verify meaningful model workloads including a quantized transformer block, multiple hardware implementations, weight/data provenance, fine-tuning capsule, fork rejection, private verification, and energy overhead
requirements.evidence: The bounded quantized single-head transformer has checked-i128 and binary64 CPU execution, independent Python replay, and a physically replayed AMD GPU compute-shader implementation with zero certified quantized error. It binds weight/source/dependency/data provenance and private-input/public-output commitments. Its deterministic fine-tuning transition selects a strict loss improvement, creates an isolated fork, preserves exact rollback, rejects a regression control, and is embedded in the externally challenged constitutional ceremony. A RISC Zero 3.0.6 guest privately executes the model/tokens/nonce and recomputes input/model/output commitments inside the zkVM; the preserved 256,850-byte receipt re-verifies against the fixed image ID. A hardware perf counter measured 11,049.71 package joules (9,411.24 core joules) over the complete 255.706-second proof interval, with scope and excluded discrete-GPU board power explicit.

requirements.requirement: Complete the ten-step governed self-improvement demonstration including external challenges and merge/reject
requirements.evidence: docs/governed_update/ceremony.json is a single reconstructable ten-step ceremony covering proposal, isolated branch, committed evaluation plan, approved tests, replayable evidence, regression detection, promotion request, external challenge, merge/promotion, and exact rollback. GitHub-hosted run 30686519873 at commit a6a49f80 externally replayed the exact transition, applied all seven challenge classes with fresh entropy, rejected semantic substitutions, signed the receipt with an ephemeral Ed25519 challenger, then keylessly signed it through GitHub OIDC/Sigstore. The preserved bundle verifies under pinned workflow identity with Cosign 3.0.6. The accepted candidate is promoted while a regression control is constitutionally rejected. Evidence explicitly discloses that external execution is not independent challenge authorship or general safety.

requirements.requirement: Operate a closed-loop scientific environment binding hypothesis, protocol, instruments, raw measurements, analysis, and conclusions
requirements.evidence: scripts/closed_loop_science.py now executes and independently verifies a complete real host-physics experiment. It commits the hypothesis, adaptive protocol, variables, acceptance/falsification rules before observation; captures signed CMOS RTC, NTP calibration, realtime, and monotonic raw observations; selects a deterministic SHA-256 intervention from the first measured uncertainty through the preregistered rule; executes and replays the intervention; captures the second instrument state; derives the bounded analysis and conclusion; and seals the entire lineage. docs/closed_loop_science_conformance.json is a successful physical run, and re-sealed raw-measurement, adaptive-decision, intervention-output, and conclusion mutations fail.

requirements.requirement: Federate specialized intelligences under interoperable proofs, privacy, institutional authority, branch competition, and challenge
requirements.evidence: A fail-closed federation ledger requires at least three distinct signed authorities and specializations, scoped institutional policies and privacy jurisdictions, capsule/proof/PROV/in-toto identities, selective-disclosure evidence commitments, all seven Observatory challenge classes, a challenger distinct from the issuer, and a third-party adjudicator distinct from both. It preserves unresolved competing branches instead of silently merging them; signature, specialization, and private-evidence mutation tests pass, with a standalone verifier.
requirements.gap: The demonstration uses locally generated keys and declared institution names; no independently governed institutions or deployed nodes have participated, as the protocol's non-claim explicitly states.

requirements.requirement: Carry scientific conclusions with literature/data dependencies, instruments, calibration, protocols, raw measurements, code, receipts, statistics, alternatives, failed replications, confirmations, and falsifiers
requirements.evidence: ProofCarryingScientificConclusion requires a sealed hypothesis/conclusion core with literature and dataset dependencies, instrument and calibration identities, preregistered protocol, raw measurements, analysis code, computation receipts, statistical assumptions, alternative explanations, confidence, and falsification conditions. It cannot assemble without distinct institution-key-signed receipts containing at least one confirmation and one failed replication; signature, discrepancy, and cross-core mutation fail. Its non-claim distinguishes evidence lineage from automatic truth.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate provenance-bound use in medicine, engineering, law, policy, or equivalent consequential institutions
requirements.evidence: None
requirements.gap: Requires domain partners, data, authorization, validation, and governance.

requirements.requirement: Preserve selective disclosure, minimization, expiry, revocation, offline verification, fork rights, pluralism, independent implementations, contestation, anti-coercion, and proof/truth separation
requirements.evidence: Selective disclosure, minimization, expiry/revocation, local verification, forks, constitutional appeal/exit, explicit proof/truth non-claims, and a three-key multi-specialization federation protocol that retains contested branches are implemented and mutation tested.
requirements.gap: The authority keys and institution identities remain locally controlled fixtures; genuine institutional pluralism, independent implementations, human contestation, and a validated anti-coercion procedure are not established.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate broadly superior intelligence through externally valid comparisons rather than self-declaration
requirements.evidence: Narrow synthetic and ARC results; repository explicitly disclaims general or superhuman intelligence
requirements.gap: No broad general-intelligence or superhuman benchmark evidence.
